title: Module C.1 — Deterministic Evidence Score
description: Output of the evidence scorer: one document per (repository, skill) pair. `confidence` is written to REPOSITORY_SKILL.confidence. Every score carries the signal values and the weights that produced it, so any number can be decomposed back to raw facts rather than defended with 'the model said so'.

confidence.description: The Evidence Score: weighted sum of the signals below, divided by the sum of applied weights. Means 'strong observable evidence exists', NOT 'probability the candidate knows the skill'.

formula_version.description: Identifies the weight set and normalisation rules used. Two rows with the same formula_version are comparable; across versions they are not.

weights.description: System-defined, never model-generated. w_llm exists because the idea doc lists six signals but only five formula terms; default it to 0 to keep LLM text out of the arithmetic, or give it a weight and say so explicitly.

llm.description: Module B's natural-language evidence, present for auditability whether or not w_llm is non-zero.

nl_evidence.description: Copied from Module B; written to SKILL_EVIDENCE.evidence and shown to the recruiter.

source.description: Exact inputs this score was computed from, for reproducibility.

detail.description: Human-readable reason for the value, e.g. 'python = 82% of repo bytes' or 'fastapi found in requirements.txt'.

matches.description: The concrete things that fired: package names, import lines, README terms.

applied.description: false when the signal is not meaningful for this skill (e.g. language % for Docker). Unapplied signals are excluded from both numerator and denominator rather than scored as 0.
